learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Omission is available and is not scored as a selected misconception.

items.title: Starting check: reject determinism
items.prompt: A temperament tendency is moderately heritable, but supportive routines reduce the associated behavior. Which conclusion is best?
options: Heredity contributes, while environment can alter expression
The behavior is genetically fixed and cannot change across environments
Supportive routines erase every form of inherited behavioral variation
Temperament has no biological contribution in the studied population
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: identify interaction
items.prompt: An inherited sensitivity predicts stress behavior in unpredictable settings but not in stable settings. What pattern is shown?
options: A purely environmental effect identical for everyone
A heredity–environment interaction in behavioral expression
A fixed genetic outcome unaffected by setting
A random outcome unrelated to either measured factor
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: separate tendency from outcome
items.prompt: Which statement best describes temperament in a multilevel behavioral explanation?
options: A complete diagnosis based on one observed response
A social condition with no biological contribution
A disposition whose expression can vary with experience
A fixed behavior that appears identically in all settings
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: experience matters
items.prompt: Siblings share many inherited factors but develop different practice histories and skill levels. Which explanation is most defensible?
options: Shared heredity guarantees identical practiced behavior
Different practice proves heredity contributes nothing
Skill differences must be measurement error only
Both shared heredity and different experience may contribute
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: interpret heritability carefully
items.prompt: A trait varies partly with inherited differences in one population. Which inference remains valid?
options: Inherited variation contributes under the studied conditions
Every individual's trait level is fixed at conception
A single gene completely determines the observed trait
Changing the environment cannot change the population pattern
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: compare environments
items.prompt: The same inherited risk score predicts high impulsive behavior after chronic sleep loss but weakly predicts behavior with regular sleep. What best explains the result?
options: Sleep alone creates identical behavior in all people
Inherited susceptibility interacts with sleep environment
The risk score determines behavior regardless of sleep
The pattern eliminates any inherited contribution
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair deterministic inference
items.prompt: Which wording correctly bounds a heredity claim about behavior?
options: Inherited factors guarantee the outcome in every setting
Environment is irrelevant whenever heritability is nonzero
Inherited variation may contribute under stated conditions
One observed behavior reveals the person's complete genotype
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: coaching and disposition
items.prompt: A partly heritable attention disposition predicts errors before coaching, but structured practice reduces errors. Which conclusion fits?
options: Coaching proves the disposition was never heritable
The disposition fixes error rate across all experiences
Structured practice changes the person's inherited sequence
Heredity contributes while experience modifies performance
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair interaction recognition
items.prompt: What observation is required to support an interaction rather than two additive main effects?
options: One factor's effect changes across levels of the other
Both factors correlate separately with the outcome
Only one factor is measured in a single setting
The outcome has the same mean in every condition
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: stress exposure
items.prompt: A temperament score predicts withdrawal strongly after repeated social stress but minimally without that stress. Which explanation is best?
options: Temperament guarantees withdrawal in every environment
Temperament and stress interact in behavioral expression
Social stress has an identical effect at every temperament level
The pattern proves temperament has no inherited component
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Starting check: define adaptive value
items.prompt: In a predator-rich habitat, a vigilance behavior is associated with more surviving offspring. What does adaptive value refer to here?
options: A conscious decision by the organism to alter inherited information
How pleasant the vigilant behavior feels to the individual organism
The behavior's contribution to reproductive success in that habitat
The behavior's universal reproductive benefit in every possible habitat
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: selection requirements
items.prompt: Which combination permits natural selection to change a behavioral distribution across generations?
options: Identical behavior and identical reproductive success
Random practice differences within one individual's life
Acquired behavior without any population variation
Heritable variation with differential reproductive success
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: regulatory gene role
items.prompt: Which statement best describes how a regulatory gene can influence behavior?
options: It alters timing or level of expression in developmental pathways
It encodes every step of one complete social behavior
It consciously selects the organism's preferred response
It removes all environmental influence from development
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: natural-population evidence
items.prompt: Which finding most directly supports genetically based behavioral variation in a natural population?
options: All individuals display identical behavior after the same single exposure
Behavioral differences persist partly across related lineages in shared conditions
Groups occupy different habitats without shared-condition inheritance data
Behavior changes immediately after a food reward during one session
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: context-specific fitness
items.prompt: A bold foraging pattern yields more offspring when food is scarce but fewer offspring when predators are abundant. Which conclusion fits?
options: Predators cannot influence reproductive success
Boldness is universally adaptive in all environments
Its adaptive value depends on the environmental context
The behavior has no possible inherited component
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: predict a population shift
items.prompt: During repeated droughts, birds with a heritable water-conserving foraging pattern leave more offspring. What population change is most expected?
options: Each bird intentionally rewrites inherited information during the drought
Every individual immediately adopts the pattern despite existing variation
All environmental influences disappear from the population after one generation
The associated heritable pattern becomes more common across generations
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair adaptive reasoning
items.prompt: Which outcome is the relevant test of adaptive value in the stated environment?
options: Whether it improves relative reproductive success
Whether the organism reports enjoying it
Whether the behavior appears complicated
Whether every species displays the behavior
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: seasonal behavior
items.prompt: A seasonal nesting behavior increases surviving offspring only in colder regions. Which statement is best?
options: The behavior is adaptive in every climate and every nesting environment
Its adaptive value is conditional on regional climate
Cold regions remove all environmental influence on reproductive success
The climate pattern rules out any possible heritable contribution
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair levels of selection explanation
items.prompt: How does differential reproductive success change a population across generations?
options: Every behavior becomes genetically identical after one event
Individuals acquire the needed inherited variant by effort
Variants linked to more offspring increase in relative frequency
Regulatory genes stop responding to developmental conditions
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: nesting depth
items.prompt: A heritable deep-nesting tendency yields more surviving offspring after many hot seasons. What is the strongest prediction?
options: Every bird changes nesting depth before reproducing
The inherited tendency must benefit birds in every climate
Hot seasons prove the tendency is entirely environmental
Deep-nesting tendency increases in the population over generations
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Starting check: prenatal order
items.prompt: Which sequence correctly orders the broad prenatal periods?
options: Germinal → embryonic → fetal
Embryonic → fetal → germinal
Fetal → germinal → embryonic
Germinal → fetal → embryonic
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Guided practice: foundational formation
items.prompt: Which broad prenatal period is most associated with foundational body-plan and organ formation?
options: Adolescent period after puberty begins
Embryonic period of foundational formation
Germinal period around implantation
Fetal period of later growth and maturation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Less help: motor development
items.prompt: Which factor combination best explains broad gains in voluntary motor control?
options: Vocabulary growth without any physiological change
A fixed timetable unaffected by experience or variation
Nervous-system maturation, strength, coordination, and practice
One exact age that applies diagnostically to every child
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: On your own: adolescent physiology
items.prompt: Which change belongs most directly to the physiological context of adolescence?
options: Implantation into the uterine lining during the germinal period
Initial prenatal tissue development before the fetal growth period
Foundational prenatal organ formation during the embryonic period
Puberty-related endocrine activation and growth changes
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Near exit: distinguish fetal emphasis
items.prompt: Which description best matches the fetal period at the required psychological-development depth?
options: Growth and maturation after foundational structures form
Conception followed immediately by implantation only
Puberty-related endocrine activation after childhood
A fixed schedule for diagnosing later motor disorders
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Changed exit: integrate sequence and behavior
items.prompt: A vignette describes endocrine activation, a growth spurt, and changing body composition. Which developmental explanation is best?
options: It describes implantation into the uterine lining during the germinal period
It reflects adolescent physiological change that can shape behavioral context
It proves a clinical developmental disorder from the timing evidence alone
It describes foundational prenatal organ formation during the embryonic period
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair developmental sequencing
items.prompt: Which cue best distinguishes embryonic from fetal development at this scope?
options: Whether puberty-related endocrine activation has already begun
Whether a motor milestone occurs at one exact diagnostic age
Foundational formation versus later growth and maturation
Whether a formal clinical diagnosis has already been assigned
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: prenatal growth
items.prompt: A prenatal description emphasizes substantial size increase and maturation of already established structures. Which period fits best?
options: Adolescence
Germinal
Embryonic
Fetal
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Repair bounded developmental inference
items.prompt: Which conclusion is appropriate when pubertal timing varies among healthy adolescents?
options: Broad sequences can coexist with individual timing variation
Every timing difference establishes a clinical disorder
Physiological development has no relation to behavior
One exact age must define normal development for everyone
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: motor-control context
items.prompt: A child gains steadier reaching after neural control, strength, and repeated practice improve. Which explanation is best?
options: Practice alone changes behavior with no physiological contribution
Motor development reflects interacting maturation and experience
One reaching observation establishes a clinical diagnosis
The change belongs specifically to prenatal implantation
items.directions: Choose the best-supported answer, then commit once. You may omit rather than guess.
